clue.text: Closely contained action worked out on a limited scale

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means shut in or closely confined

indicators.note: something worked out is solved or rearranged, so the letters of action are shuffled

explanation.surface: Some tightly confined activity is planned on a small scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scale' looks like a measure of size, but it is a musical scale; 'Closely contained' as one phrase means pent-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentatonic scale has only five notes per octave, so music written in it is limited in its range of notes.

clue.text: Put in power and run this type of current about?

definitions.text: Put in power and run this type of current about?

parts.note: to elect someone is to vote them into office
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
I is the physics symbol for ... current
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A question about voting someone into office and running a kind of current.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: power, run and current all suggest electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric current is the kind that power stations put into the mains, run round circuits.

clue.text: Male to male

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for male; the letters running across the words to male are a coincidence of the charade, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: A terse phrase about something passing from one man to another.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom is a male animal, especially a male cat.

clue.text: What ultimately is keeping this compiler?

definitions.text: What ultimately is keeping this compiler?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word What
keeping means the word is holds another piece inside it

parts.note: a setter refers to themselves as this compiler, giving me

explanation.surface: The setter wonders aloud what is keeping them in work.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is the newspaper that printed this puzzle, so the whole clue also describes the answer: the paper keeps its compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times newspaper employs and prints the crossword compiler, so it keeps them in work.

clue.text: Get flummoxed, having new place in mind

indicators.note: in tells us the new place pieces sit inside the word for mind

parts.note: nous, from Greek, means mind or intellect

explanation.surface: Someone is confused because they are thinking of moving house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' is used in the sense of baffle, as in 'that really gets me', so 'Get flummoxed' is read as one idea of perplexing.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to puzzle or baffle them so they do not know what to do.

clue.text: Puzzle of polar explorer finding wife in short trousers

indicators.note: in tells us the explorer and his wife sit together within the trousers
short means the last letter of the trousers word is cut off

parts.note: cords are corduroy trousers

indicators.note: finding joins the explorer to his wife, who comes straight after him

parts.note: James Clark Ross was a British polar explorer

explanation.surface: A puzzle about an Antarctic explorer finding his wife wearing cut-off trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts CORDS to CORD; 'finding' puts W right after ROSS. ROSS is James Clark Ross of the Ross Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword is a kind of word puzzle, like the one being solved.

clue.text: Very curious numbers must lead to Ptolemy's conclusion

indicators.note: conclusion points to the final letter of Ptolemy

explanation.surface: Numbers lead on to the end of the ancient astronomer's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must lead to' simply places NOS before the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosy person is prying, overly curious about others' business.

clue.text: Introduction of noxious anaesthetic drug brings down country

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ether was an early general anaesthetic
to land something, like an aircraft, is to bring it down

explanation.surface: A toxic anaesthetic drug fells a whole nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drug' is a link describing the anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Netherlands is a European country, also known as Holland.

clue.text: Gems of singular hues

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
tones are shades or hues of colour

explanation.surface: Gemstones of a unique colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious stones are gems, such as rubies and emeralds.

clue.text: Director on board of old rail company, introduced to chap with real power

indicators.note: introduced to means one piece is put inside another

parts.note: a he-man is a strong, virile man
the LMS was the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, an old British rail company

explanation.surface: A company director of a former railway firm meets a powerful man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' looks like membership of a board of directors, but it means aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The helmsman steers a ship, directing its course while on board.

clue.text: The right to choose work style to keep one involved

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: to keep means the style word holds one inside

parts.note: ton means fashion or style
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A choice of working method that keeps everyone engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: TON for style is an old word for fashion, as in 'the ton'.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is a choice, or the right to make one, as in a financial option.

clue.text: English artist is striking, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that we hear the word rather than read it

parts.note: stubs, as in stubs one's toe, means is striking

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that an English painter is impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' looks like 'impressive', but here it means hitting. George STUBBS was an English painter famous for horses.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stubbs was an eighteenth-century English painter, best known for horse portraits.

clue.text: Clue solver's way which might be adapted to break setter?

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters of break and setter are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tip on how the solver might crack the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'clue solver' is Sherlock Holmes, who lived at BAKER STREET in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional detective Sherlock Holmes, a solver of clues, lived at 221B on this London street.

clue.text: Auditor left altered entries

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters of entries are rearranged

explanation.surface: An accountant leaves amended entries in the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant, but it is just a hearer; 'altered' turns ENTRIES into ISTENER.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor in its literal sense is a hearer, someone who listens.

clue.text: Support for worker going to Guernsey or Jersey

definitions.text: Support for worker going to Guernsey or Jersey

parts.words: Support for worker going to Guernsey or Jersey
parts.note: the worker is a dairy hand, and Guernsey and Jersey are breeds of cow, not the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Some aid for a labourer travelling to the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Guernsey and Jersey seem to be Channel Islands (or knitted jumpers), but they are breeds of dairy cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged seat used by someone drawing milk from a cow by hand.

clue.text: Unpleasant behaviour, as can get head coming round

indicators.note: coming round means the word for head surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a ness is a headland, a promontory
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Someone recovers consciousness, as it were, after a knock on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like the top of the body, but it is a headland. 'get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastiness is unkindness or spitefulness, unpleasant conduct towards others.

clue.text: Deluge came down as late matches are played?

parts.note: a deluge is a flood
lit means alighted or landed, came down

explanation.surface: Heavy rain fell as evening games went on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came down' looks like rain falling, but LIT is landed, as a bird lights on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening matches are lit by banks of floodlights, so they are played floodlit.

clue.text: Ungodly siren broadcast in a booming manner

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of the fodder are dispersed

explanation.surface: A wicked siren is heard over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like a radio transmission, but it scatters UNGODLY SIREN.
explanation.definitionFit: Resoundingly means loudly and echoingly, as a booming sound fills a space.

clue.text: Mandolin, perhaps, wrongly placed in lutes

indicators.note: wrongly placed means the letters of in lutes are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mandolin has been misfiled among the lutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mandolin' suggests a musical instrument, but a mandoline (also spelt mandolin) is a kitchen slicer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandolin is a kitchen gadget for slicing vegetables, an example of a culinary tool.

clue.text: Outside home, what's used for walking doggy

indicators.note: Outside means the walking aid goes round the word for home

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
in means at home

explanation.surface: Outside the house, someone needs a stick for walking the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Canine means relating to dogs, doglike.

clue.text: One may find some workers like this break period

definitions.text: One may find some workers like this

parts.note: to part is to break or separate
a time is a period

explanation.surface: A worker finds a gap in the day for a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Some employees work only part of the week, so they are described as part-time staff.

clue.text: Commonwealth capital has something beneficial on both sides of the street

indicators.note: on both sides of means the boon wraps around the street

parts.note: a boon is a blessing, something beneficial

explanation.surface: A Commonwealth capital city has something good all along its street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonwealth' suggests the British Commonwealth, but Massachusetts calls itself a Commonwealth, and BOSTON is its capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Boston is the state capital of Massachusetts, officially a commonwealth.

clue.text: Family's line for right descent

indicators.note: line for right means one letter is swapped for the other

parts.note: a brood is a family of young

explanation.surface: A family's ancestry is traced for the rightful line of succession.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood means lineage or ancestry, as in being of royal blood.

clue.text: Warship builder's beginning to anger me

indicators.note: beginning points to the first letter of builder

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: A shipbuilder's first move is to make the speaker angry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bireme was an ancient galley with two banks of oars, a warship.

clue.text: Increase in importance for cocktail

definitions.meaning: to grow rapidly, gathering size and significance like a ball rolled in snow
a drink of advocaat and lemonade

explanation.surface: A drink that grows in stature.
explanation.definitionFit: To snowball is to grow ever faster; a snowball is also a cocktail of advocaat and lemonade.

clue.text: Only manservant's top half?

indicators.note: top half means the first three of its six letters, the upper part in a down entry

parts.note: a butler is the chief manservant of a household

explanation.surface: Just the upper part of a male servant.
explanation.definitionFit: But means only, as in 'there is but one way'.

clue.text: Check carefully about son's undergarment

indicators.note: about means the checking word goes around the other letter

parts.note: to vet is to examine carefully
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent inspects their son's underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A vest is a sleeveless undergarment worn on the upper body in Britain.

clue.text: Very good pie crust, say, with chips

parts.note: so is used for very good, as in agreement
the lid of a pie is its top crust
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A fine pie crust served with chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with chips' looks like a plate of fried potatoes, but solid-state devices use silicon chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid-state electronics are built from semiconductor chips rather than valves.
